title: Group Anagrams
description:
Given an array of strings `strs`, group all **anagrams** together. You may return the groups in **any order**, and the strings within each group may also be in **any order**.

An **anagram** is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, using all the original letters exactly once. Duplicate strings are anagrams of each other and must each appear in the resulting group with their original multiplicity.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Two strings are anagrams if and only if they have the exact same character frequencies (or identical sorted character sequences).
Use a canonical signature for each string as the key in a hash map whose value is the list of strings sharing that signature.
Using a 26-element letter count tuple/key avoids sorting each string and achieves O(n * k) time where k is the maximum string length.

examples.explanation: "eat", "tea", and "ate" share the letter counts {a:1, e:1, t:1}; "tan" and "nat" share {a:1, n:1, t:1}; "bat" forms its own group.
A single empty string forms a single group containing [""].
A single-character string forms a single group [["a"]].
